Credential-freeness is achieved, but §1's fail-closed \"credential file must resolve outside the repo\" (plus ownership/mode/symlink) enforcement is now unenforced at load time for `draft`. Compensating controls hold: resolveCredentials/validateCredentialFileHandle re-enforces repoContains on the open descriptor for every credential-consuming command, doctor enforces it, `kstack-config.mjs validate` (no command supplied) enforces it, and validateJiraConfig still enforces path.isAbsolute for draft — so no credential can be transmitted under a violating config. The loss is detection coverage only. Cheap fix if desired: keep the filesystem-free lexical checks (absolute + path.relative(repoRoot, source.path) not inside repo) for `draft`, and skip only the checks that require the file to exist (realpath/lstat/stat/ownership/mode) — that preserves the missing/unreadable-file tolerance the fix needed while restoring the in-repo detection."}],"materialDissent":[],"recommendation":"Approve this round's remediation. All four round-4 findings are correctly fixed, and I found no regression of the rounds 1-3 fixes.\n\nFix verification (observed in the supplied files):\n1. Credential-free draft — `validateCredentialFileConfig` (kstack-config.mjs) now performs only realpathSync/lstatSync/statSync plus dev/ino, ownership and mode checks; there is no open/read/JSON.parse of the credential file anywhere in the config path, and the call site is gated by `options.command !== 'draft'`. `loadJiraState` threads `command` through, and the CLI passes `parsed.command`. Content-level validation (UTF-8 decode, JSON.parse, exactly {email,token}) lives only in `resolveCredentials`, whose malformed-JSON and bad-UTF-8 paths now emit fixed strings ('credential file is invalid JSON' / 'credential file must be valid UTF-8') with no parser-message interpolation; the outer catch rethrows JiraQueueError before the sanitize-interpolating fallback, so those fixed strings actually reach the caller. Tests cover missing/unreadable/malformed for draft and the deferred-content case for doctor/submit, including the exit-8 wrapping ('could not re-resolve credentials: credential file is invalid JSON') with an explicit assertion that the partial-secret content does not appear.\n2. Release-fencing observability — `withDraftLock`'s finally keeps the action error primary (preserving its exit code) and attaches `actionError.releaseError`; the test asserts both the STATE_ERROR primary and the LOCK_FENCED_CLEAN releaseError.\n3. `runVerification` credentials guard — placed immediately after the direct-evidence early return, checks non-empty string email and token, fails EXIT.CONFIG_INVALID with a descriptive message instead of reaching `authorizationHeader(null)`. I traced both `credentials: null` call sites (reconcile-from-submitting with a posted:true+key covering sidecar, and the unknown-state direct-evidence branch): both are dominated by conditions that guarantee the direct-evidence early return fires, and `resolve` is refused from `submitting`, so the acknowledged/dismissed path cannot retire that evidence mid-recovery. The guard is genuinely defensive-only, which is the right shape.\n4. Doc/code alignment — JIRA_QUEUE.md now says direct evidence after `discarded` \"can only be acknowledged with `--issue-key`, never dismissed with `--distinct`; the audit-only acknowledgment does not revive the draft.\" That matches `resolveDraft`: `--distinct` fails when `hasDirectEvidence`, and `--issue-key` on a `discarded` draft falls through every state-transition branch (discarded is excluded from both the transition list and the wrong-state fail), writing only `duplicate-acknowledged` with `discardedDraftEvidenceOnly: true`.\n\nNon-regression spot checks (all still present and correct): `youngestMarkerAgeMs` returns 0 on unparseable/absent timestamps (fail-closed, test-covered on both sides of the 30s boundary with an injected clock); `verifyClearMinimumAgeMs` uses the injected clock consistently; descriptor-bound credential TOCTOU defence (O_NOFOLLOW, /proc/self/fd realpath, dev/ino recheck) with the path-swap test; FIFO fail-fast via pre-open lstat isFile + O_NONBLOCK; doctor `/myself` identity assertion with the hidden-email accountId warning; `--distinct` provenance partition via `resolutionCandidatesByProvenance`; boundedSearch's `matches` vs `inconclusive` kinds with the `complete` flag and the minimum inter-probe spacing that prevents a slow first probe from bursting the rest; `credentialHardeningWarnings`; `coveredByAbortRecovery` requiring both `posted:false` and `responseClass: 'aborted-before-post'` plus attemptId/lockId correlation; release-path sidecar writes with clean/dirty/break-race exit differentiation and `handoffWritten` correctly suppressing lock removal for a lock we no longer own.\n\n`sanitize()` in kstack-provider-runner.mjs is byte-identical to the previously reviewed version; Basic-auth, ATATT, gh*/sk-, xox*, AKIA, labeled secret/token/password, and Bearer [REDACTED] are all present, and the janitor redaction test asserts a Basic-auth-shaped responseClass is redacted before it reaches the persisted draft.\n\nFollow-ups (neither blocking): (a) the SEC-R5-1 lexical-check restoration above, if the owner wants §1's outside-repo enforcement to remain universal; (b) a one-word robustness nit — `actionError.releaseError = releaseError` throws in strict-mode ESM if a non-object is ever thrown, which would swap out the primary error inside a finally; every throw in this codebase is an Error, so this is theoretical, but `if (actionError && typeof actionError === 'object')` makes it free.","strongestObjection":"The `draft` fix is broader than the finding required: rather than removing only the content read, it removes the entire §1 credential-path validation for that command, so a credential file misconfigured to live inside the repository (commit-eligible) draws no error from the one command the skills actually invoke. I judged this low rather than blocking because the fail-closed guarantee that matters — no credential is ever transmitted under a violating config — is preserved by `validateCredentialFileHandle`'s descriptor-realpath repoContains check in `resolveCredentials`, which runs for every credential-consuming command, plus doctor and the standalone config validator.
